derivations.claim: Choose an integral basis of $L$ and let $B$ be the integer $n\times n$ matrix whose columns are the images of that basis under $f$. Since $f$ is isometric, the Gram matrix of $L$ is $B^{\mathsf T}B$. [given, A1, choose, construct]

For every path-connected topological space $X$ and $x_0\in X$, the Hurewicz map
$$h:\pi_1(X,x_0)\longrightarrow H_1(X;\mathbb Z)$$
is surjective and has kernel $[\pi_1(X,x_0),\pi_1(X,x_0)]$. Hence it induces a natural isomorphism
$$\pi_1(X,x_0)^{\mathrm{ab}}\cong H_1(X;\mathbb Z).$$
The proof is choice-free and requires no CW, separation, local path-connectivity or local simple-connectivity assumption.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms
$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$
for every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a closed smooth
manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Then $M$ has the homotopy type of a finite
CW complex ([[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]).

Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth four-manifold. Its integral intersection lattice is the abelian group $L_X=H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ with the integer-valued symmetric bilinear pairing $Q_X(\bar x,\bar y)=\langle \operatorname{PD}^{-1}(x)\smile\operatorname{PD}^{-1}(y),[X]\rangle$. Here $\operatorname{Tor}$ is the subgroup of elements of finite order, $[X]\in H_4(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the orientation class, and $\operatorname{PD}:H^2(X;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ is the Poincaré duality isomorphism. The rank is $b_2(X)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(X;\mathbb Q)$. The lattice is positive definite when $Q_X(x,x)>0$ for every nonzero $x\in L_X$; it is unimodular when a Gram matrix in an integral basis has determinant $1$ or $-1$.

derivations.claim: By [F1] and [A1], $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)=0$, so the Ext term in [F3] is zero and evaluation identifies $H^2(X;\mathbb Z)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(H_2(X;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)$. [given, F1, F3, A1, algebra]

By [F4] and [A1], $H_2(X;\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated. Its quotient $L=H_2(X;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}$ is therefore free of finite rank, and every homomorphism from $H_2$ to $\mathbb Z$ factors uniquely through $L$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}(H_2,\mathbb Z)=\operatorname{Hom}(L,\mathbb Z)$. [F4, A1, algebra]

Under the isomorphism [F2], the map $L\to\operatorname{Hom}(L,\mathbb Z)$ sending $\bar x$ to $(\bar y\mapsto Q_X(\bar x,\bar y))$ is the composite of the inverse Poincaré-duality map $H_2\to H^2$ with the evaluation map of [F3]; [F5] identifies that composite with the intersection pairing. Both component maps are isomorphisms by steps 1.1–1.2 and [F2]. Hence the pairing map is an isomorphism. [F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth Riemannian manifold of even dimension $2m$, and let $V=V^+\oplus V^-$ be a finite-rank smooth complex vector bundle with a Hermitian metric linear in its first variable. Write $\mathrm{Cl}_{\mathbb C}(T^*M,-g)$ for the complex Clifford bundle generated by cotangent vectors with relation $\xi\eta+\eta\xi=-2g^{-1}(\xi,\eta)$. A **graded Hermitian Clifford action** is a smooth real-linear map $c:T^*M\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb C}(V)$ such that $c(\xi)^*=-c(\xi)$, $c(\xi)V^\pm\subseteq V^\mp$, and $c(\xi)c(\eta)+c(\eta)c(\xi)=-2g^{-1}(\xi,\eta)I$. It extends complex-linearly to the complex Clifford bundle.

A **graded Hermitian Clifford connection** is a unitary connection $\nabla^V$ preserving $V^\pm$ and satisfying
$$\nabla^V_X(c(\xi)v)=c(\nabla^{LC}_X\xi)v+c(\xi)\nabla^V_Xv$$
for smooth $X,\xi,v$, where $\nabla^{LC}$ is the Levi–Civita connection. In a local orthonormal coframe $(e^i)$ define
$$D_Vv=\sum_i c(e^i)\nabla^V_{e_i}v.$$
The operator is odd, so its chiral part is $D_V^+:C^\infty(V^+)\to C^\infty(V^-)$. Under Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the formula's frame independence, formal symmetry on closed $M$, and global bundle well-definedness are proved in [[lem-geometric-dirac-operator-is-well-defined]]. A domain and index are assigned only under the compact hypotheses of later items.

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold of even dimension $n=2m\ge2$ with a specified Spin lift $P\to P_{SO}(TM)$. Let $S_0$ be the complex irreducible Clifford module of dimension $2^m$ supplied by [[thm-complex-spin-modules-and-compact-reducibility]], with positive-square complex Clifford action $c_+$ and full-even Spin representation $\sigma$. Put $c_0(v)=i\,c_+(v)$ for the negative-square cotangent action. This changes the Clifford square sign and preserves equivariance under $\sigma$, since the scalar $i$ commutes with that action. Define the complex spinor bundle by the associated real bundle $P\times_{\operatorname{Spin}(n)}(S_0)_{\mathbb R}$ using the realification of $\sigma$, and descend multiplication by $i$ and the Clifford action through their commuting transition maps.

For an oriented orthonormal basis $(e_1,\ldots,e_{2m})$, define the chirality operator on $S_0$ by $\Gamma_{S_0}=i^m c_0(e^1)\cdots c_0(e^{2m})$. The calculation below proves that this is basis-independent, squares to $1$, and anticommutes with each $c_0(\xi)$. Its $\pm1$ eigenspaces are $S_0^\pm$ and their associated bundles are $S^\pm$. The Levi–Civita connection on $P_{SO}(TM)$ lifts through the differential of $\operatorname{Spin}(n)\to SO(n)$ to the **spin connection** $\widetilde\nabla^S$ on $S$. This item defines these objects; [[lem-spinor-and-clifford-associated-bundles-are-well-defined]] supplies the global bundle, metric, connection, and transition verification.

Assume full AC. On an even-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold with a supplied Spin lift, the realified associated construction in [[def-even-dimensional-spinor-bundle-chirality-and-spin-connection]] is a smooth Hermitian graded Clifford bundle with a global compatible spin connection. For any graded Hermitian Clifford module there is locally a graded factorization $V\cong S_0\widehat\otimes W$. Its local multiplicity spaces $W=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{Cl}}(S_0,V)$ and the relative curvature $F^{V/S}:=F^V-c(R^{LC})$ have transition laws for which $\operatorname{str}_W\exp(-F^{V/S}/(2\pi i))$ is a global even form. In the spin-twisted case $V=S\widehat\otimes E$, this relative curvature is the curvature $F^E$ of the supplied unitary connection. For the zero-dimensional relative statement, use the orientation-graded reference line of [[def-ahat-and-relative-chern-character-forms]]; this does not construct a Spin$(0)$ lift.

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact, boundaryless, oriented Riemannian manifold of even dimension $2m$ with $m\ge0$, and let $V=V^+\oplus V^-$ be a finite-rank graded Hermitian Clifford module with compatible connection as in [[def-graded-hermitian-clifford-module-and-geometric-dirac]]. The chiral operator
$$D_V^+:H^1(M;V^+)\longrightarrow L^2(M;V^-)$$
is Fredholm and its complex index is
$$\operatorname{ind}(D_V^+)=\int_M\left[\widehat A(TM,\nabla^{LC})\operatorname{ch}(V/S)\right]_{2m}.$$
The integral is with the stated orientation. For $m=0$, write $\varepsilon_x\in\{1,-1\}$ for the orientation sign at $x$. Use the reference line $S_{0,x}=\mathbb C$ with grading $\Gamma_{S_{0,x}}=\varepsilon_xI$ and multiplicity grading $\Gamma_{W_x}=\varepsilon_x\Gamma_{V_x}$ from [[def-ahat-and-relative-chern-character-forms]]. The relative curvature is zero and the degree-zero integrand is $\varepsilon_x(\dim V_x^+-\dim V_x^-)$. The given grading of $V$ remains arbitrary, and no Spin lift is required. The result is a complex index; it makes no real KO-index assertion.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, of real dimension at least two. Its metric defines the $L^2$ pairing on forms by the Riemannian density; orientation is unnecessary. Let $d^*$ denote the formal adjoint of $d$, and $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$ on total real forms, or on their complexification. With domain $H^2$ the operator is nonnegative and selfadjoint. Its degreewise smooth kernels $\mathcal H^k$ are finite dimensional, and there is an orthogonal smooth decomposition
$$\Omega^k(M)=\mathcal H^k\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d\Omega^{k-1}(M)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d^*\Omega^{k+1}(M).$$
The map $h\mapsto[h]$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal H^k\to H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$, over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ as appropriate.

More generally let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension $m\ge1$ with a smooth Hermitian metric. Let $E$ be a holomorphic bundle of finite rank with a smooth Hermitian metric. The holomorphic bundle structure supplies frames with holomorphic invertible transition matrices; the Hermitian metric is separate smooth positive-definite pairing data. On $E$-valued $(p,q)$ forms, define $\bar\partial_E$ by the coefficientwise Dolbeault operator in holomorphic bundle charts and let $\bar\partial_E^*$ be its formal adjoint. For each fixed $p$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ on the sum over $q$ is nonnegative and selfadjoint on $H^2$; its smooth harmonic spaces $\mathcal H_E^{p,q}$ are finite dimensional and
$$\Omega^{p,q}(X,E)=\mathcal H_E^{p,q}\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E\Omega^{p,q-1}(X,E)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E^*\Omega^{p,q+1}(X,E).$$
In particular harmonic forms represent the smooth Dolbeault quotient
$$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(X,E):=\ker\bar\partial_E/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_E$$
uniquely. Terms outside the degree range are zero. This asserts smooth Dolbeault cohomology; an identification with sheaf cohomology requires a separate Dolbeault-resolution comparison theorem.

For either complex write $D=d$ or $D=\bar\partial_E$, $P=DD^*+D^*D$, and let $\Pi,G$ be the preceding Green projection and inverse. They preserve degree, $G$ preserves smooth forms, and on smooth forms
$$DG=GD,\qquad D^*G=GD^*,\qquad D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0.$$
Every closed smooth $u$ satisfies $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold $M$, possibly with boundary, integration on smooth simplices followed by the inverse of restriction from continuous to smooth singular cohomology gives a natural isomorphism of unital graded real algebras
$$J_M:H^*_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)\xrightarrow{\cong}H^*_{\mathrm{sing}}(M;\mathbb R).$$
The source product is wedge of form classes, the target product is the front/back singular cup product, and both stars denote direct sums of the homogeneous groups. Naturality is for smooth maps. No compactness assumption is imposed.

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold,
possibly with boundary. If $E\to M$ is a rank-$r$ complex vector bundle with
complex connection $\nabla$ and curvature $\Omega$, define the total Chern form
$$c(\nabla)=\det\!\left(I-\frac{\Omega}{2\pi i}\right)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_j(\nabla),$$
where $c_j(\nabla)$ has degree $2j$. For a Hermitian connection these forms
are real-valued; a general complex connection need not give real-valued forms.

For a rank-$r$ real vector bundle with real connection $\nabla$, let
$E_{\mathbb C}=E\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ carry the complexified
connection $\nabla_{\mathbb C}$ and set
$$p_j(\nabla)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})\quad\text{in degree }4j,\qquad p(\nabla)=\sum_{j\geq0}p_j(\nabla).$$
Then $p_0=1$, $p_j=0$ when $2j>r$, and every $p_j(\nabla)$ is real-valued,
even if $\nabla$ is not metric-compatible. If $\nabla$ is compatible with a
Euclidean metric, each odd Chern form $c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ vanishes
pointwise. Assume full Axiom of Choice (AC); for every real connection each
$c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ is then exact, with AC used through existence
of a metric-compatible connection and the transgression lemma.

If $E$ is an oriented Euclidean bundle of even rank $2m$ and $\nabla$ is
metric-compatible, define
$$e(\nabla)=\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\frac{\Omega}{2\pi}\right),$$
where the Pfaffian uses the ordered oriented orthonormal frame and
$\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&a\\-a&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)=a$.
These curvature evaluations are closed forms. In rank zero,
$c(\nabla)=p(\nabla)=e(\nabla)=1$. The Euler form is defined here only for
oriented even-rank Euclidean bundles with a metric-compatible connection.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies
$$\mathcal I_M(d\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)).$$
For $n=0$ it is the finite signed sum $\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p)$. All assertions are choice-free: no partition on the entire manifold is required.

derivations.claim: Construct the required Clifford module explicitly. Put $V_0^+=\Lambda^1T^*X\otimes\mathbb C$ and $V_0^-=(\Lambda^0\oplus\Lambda^-)T^*X\otimes\mathbb C$, with their metric Hermitian forms. For a real covector $\xi$ define $B_\xi a=(-\iota_{\xi^\sharp}a,\sqrt2\,\pi_-(\xi\wedge a))$ and $c(\xi)(a,b)=(-B_\xi^*b,B_\xi a)$ on $V_0^+\oplus V_0^-$. In an oriented orthonormal frame with $\xi=te^1$, the scalar part of $B_\xi a$ has squared norm $t^2|a_1|^2$, while the three forms $\sqrt2\pi_-(e^1\wedge e^j)$, $j=2,3,4$, are orthonormal. Hence $B_\xi^*B_\xi=|\xi|^2I$. Both spaces have dimension four, so for $\xi\ne0$ also $B_\xi B_\xi^*=|\xi|^2I$; the zero case is immediate. Polarization gives the Clifford relation $c(\xi)c(\eta)+c(\eta)c(\xi)=-2\langle\xi,\eta\rangle I$, and the displayed block matrix is skew-Hermitian and odd. Wedge, contraction and $\pi_-$ are parallel for the Levi–Civita connection, so the induced connection is Clifford-compatible. Its chiral Dirac operator is exactly $\widetilde D_0=d^*\oplus\sqrt2d^-$. This is an actual geometric Clifford module, not a postulated Spin factorization.

Let $E=P\times_{SU(2)}\mathbb C^2$ and $G=\operatorname{ad}P\otimes\mathbb C$, with their induced unitary connections. The bundle $G$ is the trace-zero endomorphism bundle of $E$. Set $Z=-F_E/(2\pi i)$, a traceless two-by-two matrix of commuting two-forms. The determinant convention gives $c_2(E)=-\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}(Z^2)$ as a form. For a traceless diagonal matrix with entries $u,-u$, its commutator action on trace-zero endomorphisms has eigenvalues $0,2u,-2u$. Therefore $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{ad}Z)=0$ and $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{ad}Z)^2)=4\operatorname{tr}(Z^2)$. These are polynomial identities for all traceless complex matrices: matrices with distinct eigenvalues are dense, and continuity gives the rest. Polarizing the degree-two identity gives the same identity for matrices of two-forms. It follows, through degree four, that $\operatorname{ch}(G)=3-4c_2(E)$, with no degree-two term. This fixes the factor and sign directly from the stated Chern normalization.

Fix its chirality sign and multiplicity. Write $c_j=c(e^j)$. Applying $c_4c_3c_2c_1$ to $e^1\in V_0^+$ gives successively $(-1,0)$, $-e^2$, $(0,(e^{23}-e^{14})/\sqrt2)$, and $-e^1$. Reversal of four distinct generators has positive sign, so $c_1c_2c_3c_4e^1=-e^1$. The construction is $SO(4)$-equivariant, and oriented rotations carry $e^1$ to every unit one-form; therefore $-c_1c_2c_3c_4=I$ on $V_0^+$. This volume operator anticommutes with every $c_j$; since $c_1$ identifies the two summands, it is $-I$ on $V_0^-$. Thus the given grading IS the reference chirality $i^2c_1c_2c_3c_4$. In the local factorization in [F1], $\Gamma_{V_0}=\Gamma_S\otimes\Gamma_W$ consequently forces $\Gamma_W=I$. The local multiplicity has rank $8/4=2$ and is entirely even. If $\Theta=\operatorname{ch}(V_0/S)$, then $\Theta_0=2$. This conclusion patches without choosing a global spinor bundle.

Calibrate the untwisted index by harmonic forms, rather than import an Euler/signature index formula. On a closed manifold, $\int_Xda\wedge da=\int_Xd(a\wedge da)=0$. Since $\alpha\wedge\alpha=(|\alpha^+|^2-|\alpha^-|^2)d\mathrm{vol}$ for real two-forms, polarization and complexification give $2\|d^-a\|_2^2=\|da\|_2^2$. Hence the smooth kernel of $\widetilde D_0$ is exactly the harmonic one-forms. Its formal adjoint is $(f,\omega)\mapsto df+\sqrt2d^*\omega$, with $\omega$ anti-self-dual. Pairing this equation with $df$ gives $\|df\|_2^2=0$, because $\langle d^*\omega,df\rangle=\langle\omega,d(df)\rangle=0$. Thus $f$ is constant and $d^*\omega=0$. For an anti-self-dual two-form the latter is equivalent to $d\omega=0$, so $\omega$ is harmonic. The Dirac regularity in [F1] identifies the Hilbert kernel and cokernel with these smooth spaces. On harmonic two-forms the Hodge star preserves the space and splits the intersection form into positive and negative definite summands: its value on $\omega^++\omega^-$ is $\|\omega^+\|_2^2-\|\omega^-\|_2^2$. By [F2] their negative dimension is precisely $b_-(X)$. Consequently $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_0=b_1(X)-1-b_-(X)$.

Twist the actual module of step1.1 by $G$, with the product connection. On its local multiplicity factor the curvature is $F^{V_0/S}\otimes I+I\otimes F_G$, and the two factors commute. The finite exponential and tensor-trace identities therefore give $\operatorname{ch}((V_0\otimes G)/S)=\Theta\operatorname{ch}(G)$. The identities are invariant under the local multiplicity transitions in [F1], so they are global form identities, requiring no Spin structure. Applying the actual analytic index theorem to the twisted and untwisted modules yields $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_A=3\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_0-4\int_X\widehat A_0\Theta_0c_2(E)$. Here $\widetilde D_A=d_A^*\oplus\sqrt2d_A^-$, $\widehat A_0=1$, and $\Theta_0=2$ by step2.1. Using [F3] to evaluate the Chern form gives $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb C}\widetilde D_A=3(b_1-1-b_-)-8\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. No assertion that $d_A^2=0$ was used: the Clifford operator and its index calculation apply to every smooth connection.

Multiplication of the target summand $\Lambda^-\otimes\operatorname{ad}P$ by $\sqrt2$ is a bounded invertible map on $L^2$, so $\widetilde D_A$ and $D_A$ have the same kernel and isomorphic cokernels on their exact first-Sobolev domains. The complex operator just computed is the complexification of the real one. If a complexified equation holds, its real and imaginary parts satisfy the real equation; hence its kernel is the complexification of the real kernel, and the same holds for the orthogonal cokernel using the adjoint. Finite complex dimensions of these spaces equal the corresponding real dimensions. Closed range transfers to the real operator by restricting the complex estimate, or by taking real parts of convergent-image preimages in the kernel complement. Thus $D_A:H^1\to L^2$ is real Fredholm and has index $8k-3(1-b_1+b_-)$, with $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. This is not a claim about a KO-index theorem.

If $\pi_1(X)=0$, every closed real one-form is exact: define a primitive by path integration from a basepoint; nullhomotopy and local primitives make the integral independent of path. Thus $b_1=0$ by [F2]. Positive definiteness gives $b_-=0$, and the prescribed charge is $k=1$. The proved formula gives $8-3=5$. Full AC has entered exactly through [F1]–[F3]'s analytic index, harmonic representatives and characteristic-class comparison; the finite symbol, chirality, trace and sign calculations add no choice.

Assume full AC, using Sobolev norms formed from the $L^p$ norms of Euclidean ordered derivative tensors. There exist constants $\varepsilon,C,C_3>0$ with the following property. Let $A$ be a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued one-form on the closed Euclidean ball $B_r(0)\subset\mathbb R^4$, with Frobenius target norm and curvature $F_A=dA+A\wedge A$. If $\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_r)}\le\varepsilon$, then there exists $g:B_r\to SU(2)$ belonging to $W^{2,p}$ for every finite $p\ge2$ such that
$$a=A^g=g^{-1}dg+g^{-1}Ag,\qquad d^*a=0,$$
and $a$ belongs to the $W^{1,3}$ closure $Y_3$ of smooth one-forms with zero normal component on the sphere. In particular the normal condition is valid in the weak integration identity. The form $a$ belongs to every $W^{1,p}$ with finite $p\ge2$ and satisfies
$$r^{-1}\|a\|_2+\|\nabla a\|_2+\|a\|_4\le C\|F_A\|_2,\qquad r^{-1}\|a\|_3+\|\nabla a\|_3\le C_3\|F_A\|_3.$$
The constants are independent of $r$ and $A$; no uniform bound on the gauge's higher norms in terms of the critical curvature norm alone is asserted.

If a fixed finite $\Gamma\le O(4)$ acts on the ball and $\tau$ is an action of $\Gamma$ on $SU(2)$ by constant unitary conjugations, assume $\gamma^*A=d\tau_\gamma(A)$. Then $g$ may be chosen with $g(\gamma x)=\tau_\gamma(g(x))$. This includes prescribed conjugation actions coming from $PU(2)$ representations, without choosing a lift to an $SU(2)$ representation.

For a finite collection of balls with smooth local connection forms $A_i$ and given smooth $SU(2)$ transition maps $t_{ij}$ satisfying $A_j=A_i^{t_{ij}}$ and $t_{ij}t_{jk}=t_{ik}$, apply the construction on each ball where its curvature bound holds. The transformed maps $h_{ij}=g_i^{-1}t_{ij}g_j$ are continuous $W^{2,3}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ transition maps on the overlaps, satisfy the cocycle identities pointwise, and identify the transformed connection forms by $a_j=a_i^{h_{ij}}$.

Assume full AC. There are constants $\eta,\delta>0$ with the following property. Let $g$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on the Euclidean unit four-ball with $\|g-I\|_{C^0}<\eta$. Let $a\in W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_1;\mathfrak{su}(2)\otimes\mathbb R^4)$ satisfy the EUCLIDEAN Coulomb condition $d_e^*a=0$ and either $F_a^{+,g}=0$ or $F_a^{-,g}=0$ distributionally. Then $a$ has a smooth representative in $B_1$.

There is also a uniform interior conclusion. If a family of such metrics is bounded in every fixed $C^j$ norm on compact subballs and the forms satisfy $\|a\|_{L^4(B_1)}\le\delta$, the forms are bounded in every fixed $C^j$ norm on each compact subball, by constants depending only on that subball and the corresponding finite metric bounds. No initial bound on higher derivatives of $a$ is required.

There are also $\epsilon>0$ and constants $C_M$ such that every smooth connection $A$ near $\overline B_1$ with $F_A^{\pm,g}=0$, $\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_1)}\le\epsilon$, and $\|g\|_{C^1(B_1)}\le M$ satisfies $\|F_A\|_{L^\infty(B_{1/2})}\le C_M\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_1)}$. Curvature norms in this assertion are Euclidean coefficient norms; $\epsilon$ is independent of $A$. On a ball of radius $r$ the corresponding bound is $r^2\|F_A\|_\infty\le C_M\|F_A\|_2$, with $M$ a bound for the rescaled metric.

Consequently the assertion applies in sufficiently small normal-coordinate balls for ANY smooth Riemannian four-manifold, after dilation, whenever its small-curvature construction supplies the Euclidean Coulomb gauge in those coordinates. It supplies local regularity and interior estimates in that given gauge, not point removal, charge quantization or global compactness.

Assume full AC. Put $\mathcal A_r=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:r/2<|x|<2r\}$, with Euclidean coefficient and Frobenius matrix norms. There are universal $\delta,C>0$ such that every smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ connection form $A$ near $\overline{\mathcal A_r}$ with
$$r^2\|F_A\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A_r)}\le\delta$$
has a smooth gauge $g:\mathcal A_r\to SU(2)$ satisfying
$$\|A^g\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A_r)}\le Cr\|F_A\|_{L^\infty(\mathcal A_r)},\qquad A^g=g^{-1}dg+g^{-1}Ag.$$
No Coulomb condition or gauge bound from a curvature $L^2$ norm alone is asserted here.

Assume full AC. There exist universal $\epsilon,C>0$ such that every smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ connection form $A$ on $B_2(0)\setminus\{0\}\subset\mathbb R^4$ with Euclidean $F_A^+=0$ and $\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_2\setminus\{0\})}\le\epsilon$ admits a smooth gauge $g:B_{1/2}\setminus\{0\}\to SU(2)$ for which
$$B=A^g\in L^4(B_{1/2}),\qquad \|B\|_{L^4(B_{1/2})}\le C\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_2)},\qquad \|F_B\|_{L^2(B_{1/2})}\le\|F_A\|_{L^2(B_2)}.$$
The singleton has measure zero in these norms; no value of $B$ at zero is prescribed. The input includes only finite small curvature energy and the punctured ASD equation, not an assumed small potential gauge. No Coulomb condition or smooth extension across zero is asserted by this lemma.

Assume full AC. Let $A$ be a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ connection form on $B_1(0)\setminus\{0\}\subset\mathbb R^4$, with the standard Euclidean metric and orientation. If $F_A^+=0$ and
$$\int_{B_1\setminus\{0\}}|F_A|^2<\infty,$$
then there exist a smooth map $g:B_1\setminus\{0\}\to SU(2)$ and a smooth $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ connection form $a$ on all of $B_1$ such that $A^g=a$ on the punctured ball. The extended form satisfies $F_a^+=0$ classically. The gauge is not required to extend across zero or to satisfy a boundary condition.

The input is a connection form in a given trivialization of the punctured ball. No general curved-metric, prescribed surface singularity, perturbed ASD equation, energy quantization, Fredholm or gluing assertion is included.

Assume full AC and put $s=12/5$. Let finitely many open Euclidean balls $U_i\subset\mathbb R^4$ cover a nonempty compact set $K$. Suppose $h_{ij}$ and, for each positive integer $n$, $h_{ij}^n$ are continuous $SU(2)$ transition cocycles on this same cover, with all maps in $W^{2,s}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ on their overlaps. Assume $h_{ij}^n\to h_{ij}$ strongly in $W^{2,s}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ and uniformly on compact subsets.

There exist an open neighborhood $V$ of $K$, smaller open sets $V_i\Subset U_i$ covering $V$, an integer $n_0$, and continuous maps $\sigma_i^n:V\cap V_i\to SU(2)$ in $W^{2,s}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for every $n\ge n_0$ such that
$$h_{ij}=(\sigma_i^n)^{-1}h_{ij}^n\sigma_j^n\quad\text{on }V\cap V_i\cap V_j,\qquad \sigma_i^n\to I\text{ strongly in }W^{2,s}_{\mathrm{loc}}\text{ and uniformly on compact subsets}.$$
Thus these are explicit Sobolev isomorphisms with the fixed limiting cocycle on the smaller neighborhood.

In particular, apply this to the cocycles and connection forms $a_i^n,a_i$ constructed by [[lem-critical-coulomb-compactness-on-a-fixed-finite-ball-cover]], and to any compact $K\subset\bigcup_iU_i$. Then
$$b_i^n=(a_i^n)^{\sigma_i^n}=(\sigma_i^n)^{-1}d\sigma_i^n+(\sigma_i^n)^{-1}a_i^n\sigma_i^n$$
are connection forms with transition cocycle exactly $h_{ij}$, and $b_i^n-a_i^n\to0$ strongly in $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Consequently $b_i^n\rightharpoonup a_i$ in $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, $b_i^n\to a_i$ in every $L^p_{\mathrm{loc}}$ for $1\le p<4$, and $F_{b_i^n}\rightharpoonup F_{a_i}$ in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Euclidean anti-self-duality is preserved if present. No Coulomb or normal boundary condition for the transferred forms $b_i^n$ is asserted.

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $(U_\alpha)_{\alpha\in A}$ be a supplied
countable open cover of $M$, let $r\in\mathbb N$, and let
$g_{\beta\alpha}:U_\alpha\cap U_\beta\to GL(r,\mathbb R)$ be smooth maps
satisfying the identities of [[lem-vector-bundle-transition-functions-satisfy-the-cocycle-identities]].
Then the quotient of $\coprod_{\alpha\in A}(U_\alpha\times\mathbb R^r)$ by the
relation

$$ (p,v)_\alpha\sim (p,g_{\beta\alpha}(p)v)_\beta $$

is a smooth rank-$r$ vector bundle over $M$.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff second-countable smooth manifold,
possibly with boundary. If $E\to M$ is a rank-$r$ complex vector bundle with
complex connection $\nabla$ and curvature $\Omega$, define the total Chern form
$$c(\nabla)=\det\!\left(I-\frac{\Omega}{2\pi i}\right)=\sum_{j=0}^r c_j(\nabla),$$
where $c_j(\nabla)$ has degree $2j$. For a Hermitian connection these forms
are real-valued; a general complex connection need not give real-valued forms.

For a rank-$r$ real vector bundle with real connection $\nabla$, let
$E_{\mathbb C}=E\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb C$ carry the complexified
connection $\nabla_{\mathbb C}$ and set
$$p_j(\nabla)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})\quad\text{in degree }4j,\qquad p(\nabla)=\sum_{j\geq0}p_j(\nabla).$$
Then $p_0=1$, $p_j=0$ when $2j>r$, and every $p_j(\nabla)$ is real-valued,
even if $\nabla$ is not metric-compatible. If $\nabla$ is compatible with a
Euclidean metric, each odd Chern form $c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ vanishes
pointwise. Assume full Axiom of Choice (AC); for every real connection each
$c_{2j+1}(\nabla_{\mathbb C})$ is then exact, with AC used through existence
of a metric-compatible connection and the transgression lemma.

If $E$ is an oriented Euclidean bundle of even rank $2m$ and $\nabla$ is
metric-compatible, define
$$e(\nabla)=\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\frac{\Omega}{2\pi}\right),$$
where the Pfaffian uses the ordered oriented orthonormal frame and
$\operatorname{Pf}\!\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&a\\-a&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)=a$.
These curvature evaluations are closed forms. In rank zero,
$c(\nabla)=p(\nabla)=e(\nabla)=1$. The Euler form is defined here only for
oriented even-rank Euclidean bundles with a metric-compatible connection.

Let $M^n$ be an oriented smooth manifold without boundary. For each compact set $K\subseteq M$ there are finitely many nonnegative smooth functions $\chi_i$ with compact supports contained in connected coordinate domains $U_i$, such that $\sum_i\chi_i=1$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. For $\omega\in\Omega_c^n(M)$ define
$$\mathcal I_M(\omega)=\sum_i I_{\phi_i}(\chi_i\omega)\quad(K=\operatorname{supp}\omega),$$
using the signed chart integrals. This value is independent of the finite functions and charts. It defines a linear functional, is local under restriction to an open set containing the support, and for $n\ge1$ satisfies
$$\mathcal I_M(d\eta)=0\qquad(\eta\in\Omega_c^{n-1}(M)).$$
For $n=0$ it is the finite signed sum $\sum_{p\in\operatorname{supp}\omega}\varepsilon(p)\omega(p)$. All assertions are choice-free: no partition on the entire manifold is required.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge2$, a bounded $C^1$ domain Omega and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}F\cdot\nu\,dS$. Both integrals are finite, with the continuous interior derivative convention and the outward normal on every boundary component.

**Assume the Axiom of Choice.** Let $X$ be a nonempty compact metric space, let $Y$ be a proper metric space, and let $(f_k)_{k\in\mathbb N}$ be an equicontinuous sequence in $C(X,Y)$. If $\{f_k(x):k\in\mathbb N\}$ is bounded for every $x\in X$, then some subsequence converges uniformly to a member of $C(X,Y)$.
Let $0<r<R$ and $n\ge 1$. Then there exists a smooth function $\rho:\mathbb R^n\to [0,1]$ such that $\rho=1$ on $\overline B_r(0)$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)\subseteq B_R(0)$.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Fix finitely many positive coordinate-ball charts with compactly contained working subcharts covering $X$. A positive linear change makes the metric Euclidean at each chart center; shrink the charts so its coefficient matrix is within [F2]'s fixed small $C^0$ neighborhood throughout. For each sequence member, a frame at a chart center extends over that ball by radial parallel transport. This exists intrinsically: the ordered matrix integral series constructs transport in each bundle chart; finite subdivision of each compact path and uniqueness patch those solutions, and smooth parameter dependence makes the endpoint frame smooth. It is smooth at the center by the same local radial equation there. Thus the coordinate-ball trivializations can be chosen even for a sequence of different bundles; no common topological trivialization is being assumed. Metric energy and Euclidean coefficient energy are uniformly comparable on this finite list. List the coordinate balls with rational centers and radii whose quadrupled closures are in a chart. By successive bounded real subsequence extraction and one diagonal, arrange that the energy integral on every quadrupled listed ball has a limit. Choose $\theta>0$ so energy less than $2\theta$ on such a ball implies the Euclidean curvature smallness in [F1] and the resulting potential smallness in [F2], after dilation. Let $S$ be the points not lying in any listed ball whose quadrupled-ball limiting energy is less than $\theta$. Its complement is open. If $N$ distinct points lie in $S$, choose $N$ listed balls containing them with pairwise disjoint quadrupled closures; this is possible by the coordinate basis and finitely many positive distances. Each limiting energy is at least $\theta$, so $N\theta\le M$. Thus $S$ is finite. For every compact set in its complement finitely many good balls suffice, and all their required smallness bounds hold eventually.

On each good ball apply [F1] on its quadruple. The pulled-back form is Euclidean Coulomb, while its curvature satisfies the actual curved self-duality equation by gauge covariance. Apply [F2] on smaller subballs: the potentials have uniform bounds in every fixed derivative order on the working ball. The constructed gauges are smooth there: their weak equation $du=u a-A_nu$, with smooth $A_n,a$, first gives every local first Sobolev order and then every higher order by differentiation. On an overlap, its transformed transition $h_{ij}^n$ is unitary and satisfies $dh_{ij}^n=h_{ij}^n a_j^n-a_i^n h_{ij}^n$, with the fixed coordinate pullback on $a_j^n$ understood. This identity and the uniform local coefficient bounds give uniform derivative bounds on every smaller overlap, inductively; a bound on the transition itself is supplied by compact $SU(2)$. There is no assumption that two different coordinate charts define the same Euclidean Coulomb operator. Apply [F6] on countably many smaller compact balls, to all coefficient and transition derivatives, and diagonalize. This gives smooth limits $a_i,h_{ij}$, convergence in every local derivative norm, the transition equation and the exact cocycle identities. The latter pass pointwise by uniform convergence on triple-overlap compacts. By [F4] they define one smooth bundle $P_\infty$ and connection $A_\infty$ on $X\setminus S$. The equation passes to the smooth limits, so $F_{A_\infty}^-=0$. On each compact subset its energy is the limit of the original energy and is at most $M$.

Establish removal for the possibly nontrivial limiting bundle near a point of $S$. The needed small punctured curvature gauge has an intrinsic construction. On a dyadic coordinate annulus, choose a frame at one basepoint and transport it along the two spherical path families of [F3]'s annular proof. Transport is defined in finitely many bundle charts along each path, and its variation identity is intrinsic: the covariant derivative of the endpoint frame is the integral of transported curvature over the path variation. The two caps' transports differ by the holonomy of the same explicit spherical lune of area at most $2\pi$. Thus their quaternionic average supplies a global annular frame with potential at most $C r\|F\|_\infty$, without assuming that the punctured bundle already has a global trivialization. On a sufficiently small punctured ball, finite energy and [F2] give, for $r_j=2^{-j}$ and $E_j$ the energy on $\{r_j/4<|x|<4r_j\}$, the bounds $\|F\|_{L^\infty(\{r_j/2<|x|<2r_j\})}\le C r_j^{-2}\sqrt{E_j}$ and $\sum_jE_j\le5E$. These are applications on ordinary balls away from the puncture; all rescaled metric bounds are uniform. Make the total energy small enough for the annular threshold. Align neighboring frames by their relative value at one fixed point of each overlap, as in [F3]. The relative frame then differs from identity by at most $C(\sqrt{E_j}+\sqrt{E_{j+1}})$ on that overlap, by integrating its gauge equation along bounded-length angular/radial paths. Average these aligned frames with a dyadic partition having only adjacent overlaps and normalize their quaternionic norm. This gives ONE smooth frame on the whole punctured smaller ball. Its potential $B$ obeys $|B|\le C r_j^{-1}(\sqrt{E_j}+\sqrt{E_{j+1}})$ on the $j$th band, hence $\int|B|^4\le C\sum_j(E_j^2+E_{j+1}^2)\le CE^2$. This reconstructs the punctured $L^4$ argument for the curved metric; no Euclidean-ASD theorem is applied to $A_\infty$.

In this actual punctured frame choose smooth cutoffs $\chi_j=0$ on $B_{r_j}$ and $1$ outside $B_{2r_j}$, with $|d\chi_j|\le C/r_j$. The potentials $B_j=\chi_jB$ extended by zero are smooth on the full fixed ball. If $\mathcal F$ is the punctured curvature extended as an $L^2$ class, their exact curvatures are $F_{B_j}=\chi_j\mathcal F+d\chi_j\wedge B+(\chi_j^2-\chi_j)B\wedge B$. Holder and absolute continuity show $F_{B_j}\to\mathcal F$ in $L^2$: the cutoff derivative term is bounded by $C\|B\|_{L^4(\{r_j<|x|<2r_j\})}$ and the quadratic term by its square. Choose the punctured ball initially small enough that all these curvatures are below [F1]'s threshold. Construct full-ball Coulomb gauges $u_j$ and potentials $b_j$ with bounded $W^{1,2}$ and small $L^4$ norms. Weak Hilbert extraction and Rellich give weak $W^{1,2}$ and strong $L^p$, $p<4$, limits; the actual argument in [F3]'s point-removal proof passes $b_j\wedge b_j$ first in $L^1$ and then the bounded curvature in weak $L^2$, giving $F_b$. The $g$-anti-self-dual projections of $F_{B_j}$ tend to zero in $L^2$ because $\pi_{-,g}$ is a fixed smooth bounded coefficient operator. Unitary covariance gives the same assertion for $b_j$, so $d_e^*b=0$ and $F_b^{-,g}=0$ weakly on the ENTIRE ball. By [F2], $b$ is smooth across the point. On punctured compact sets the gauge equations $du_j=u_jb_j-Bu_j$ give bounded $W^{1,4}$ norms; Rellich and a diagonal yield a unitary limit $u$ with $du=ub-Bu$. Passing the products uses strong $L^3$ convergence of $b_j$ and strong $L^{12}$ convergence of the bounded matrices. Smooth $b,B$ bootstrap this equation to a smooth $SU(2)$ map on the puncture. Thus $B^u=b$ there. Glue a new trivial ball using this actual gauge; it extends the limiting bundle and connection smoothly. Repeat at the finitely many points of $S$, obtaining a smooth self-dual $A_\infty$ on a bundle over ALL of $X$. This is the full curved point removal argument, including its actual limiting gauge.

Construct comparison isomorphisms, not merely unrelated local gauges. On a compact core $K\Subset X\setminus S$, select finitely many working charts from step2.1 and smaller charts covering a neighborhood of $K$. Choose smooth weights $\phi_j$ with compact support in the larger charts, summing to one on that neighborhood. In chart $i$ put $T_i^n=\sum_j\phi_jh_{ij}^nh_{ji}$. Since the two transition cocycles converge smoothly on the finitely many compact supports, $T_i^n\to I$ in every derivative norm. For large $n$ its quaternionic norm is bounded below by one half. Set $\sigma_i^n=T_i^n/(\tfrac12\operatorname{tr}((T_i^n)^*T_i^n))^{1/2}$. The cocycle laws give $T_i^n=h_{ik}^nT_k^nh_{ki}$; their scalar norms agree, so $h_{ik}=(\sigma_i^n)^{-1}h_{ik}^n\sigma_k^n$. Therefore these are actual smooth bundle isomorphisms from the limiting bundle to the original one on the core neighborhood. The transferred connections $(a_i^n)^{\sigma_i^n}$ converge smoothly to $a_i$. This is [F4]'s finite averaging proof with smooth manifold weights, not its Euclidean-cover Statement outside scope.

Choose increasing cores by deleting shrinking disjoint balls about $S$. Apply step5.1 and diagonal selection so that the $n$th chosen comparison is within $1/n$ in every derivative order at most $n$ on the $n$th core. Extend each comparison to the WHOLE punctured manifold. Indeed near a deleted sphere both bundles have the smooth ball trivializations, one original and one from step4.1. On the collar the comparison is an $SU(2)$ function $h(\vartheta,r)$. Choose a smooth radial function $f(r)$ equal to $r$ on its outer collar and equal to one interior collar radius for all sufficiently small positive $r$. Then $h(\vartheta,f(r))$ extends the comparison across the remaining punctured end and agrees with it near its original domain boundary. No extension across the center is requested. Perform this on each disjoint punctured ball. These are actual bundle isomorphisms on $X\setminus S$ for each sequence member, and the extensions change nothing on the exhausting cores. Consequently the transported connections converge in $C^\infty_{\mathrm{loc}}(X\setminus S)$, in particular in the asserted local Sobolev gauges. No assertion that $P_\infty$ and $P$ extend isomorphically across $S$ has been made.

Identify the lost energy before calling it an integer. Choose disjoint coordinate balls $B_r(p)$ about the finite points of $S$ and one decreasing radius sequence tending to zero at each point. Extract further so the integrals of $|F_{A_n}|^2$ on all these balls converge. Smooth convergence on every compact annulus shows $\lim_n\int_{B_r(p)}|F_{A_n}|^2-\int_{B_r(p)}|F_{A_\infty}|^2$ is independent of these sufficiently small radii: subtract two radii and use smooth annular convergence. Denote it $\lambda_p$. It is positive. In fact, because $p$ was bad in step1.1, every neighborhood contains a listed ball containing $p$ whose limiting energy on its quadruple is at least $\theta$; choose that quadruple inside $B_r(p)$. Hence the first limiting integral is at least $\theta$, while the smooth extended connection's ball energy tends to zero as $r\to0$. Thus $\lambda_p\ge\theta>0$. For a continuous test function $f$, split its integral over these balls and their complement. On the complement use smooth convergence; on each ball replacing $f$ by $f(p)$ costs at most its oscillation there times the bounded total energy. Let their radii tend to zero. This proves actual weak energy-measure convergence to $|F_{A_\infty}|^2d\mathrm{vol}+\sum_p\lambda_p\delta_p$ and the identity $\lim_n E(A_n)=E(A_\infty)+\sum_p\lambda_p$. No bubble-tree energy identity has been assumed.

Prove individual charge quantization by clutching. Fix one sufficiently small ball $B=B_r(p)$ as in step7.1 and use the comparison from step6.1 on its fixed boundary collar. In its limiting smooth frame the transported connection $a_n$ converges smoothly to $A_\infty$ there. Modify $a_n$ by a fixed collar cutoff to equal $A_\infty$ near $\partial B$, and transport this modification back to the original frame. It defines a smooth connection $A_n'$ on the original bundle over $B$, equal to $A_n$ away from the collar. Since the modification tends to zero with all derivatives in the comparison frame, $\int_Bc_2(A_n')-\int_Bc_2(A_n)\to0$, by the actual curvature polynomial and gauge invariance. Glue this ball bundle to the oppositely oriented limiting ball bundle using the comparison on the boundary. To make the connections match smoothly, flatten each near its boundary to the product pullback of its common tangential connection. This changes neither Chern integral: for a path of connections, direct differentiation and Bianchi give $\partial_t\operatorname{tr}(F_t\wedge F_t)=2d\operatorname{tr}(\dot A_t\wedge F_t)$; a deformation fixing the tangential boundary connection has zero tangential transgression trace. Explicitly write that three-form as $\sum_i(-1)^{i-1}V_i\,dx_1\wedge\cdots\widehat{dx_i}\cdots\wedge dx_4$; its derivative is $(\operatorname{div}V)dx$ and its zero tangential trace is $V\cdot\nu=0$. The actual ball divergence theorem in [F5] therefore makes its derivative integral zero. Product collars then glue a smooth connection on an actual $SU(2)$ bundle over the doubled ball $S^4$. Its Chern number is the integer $q_n=\int_Bc_2(A_n')-\int_Bc_2(A_\infty)$. By [F5] and step7.1, $q_n\to-\lambda_p/(8\pi^2)$. A convergent integer sequence is eventually constant, so $m_p=\lambda_p/(8\pi^2)$ is an integer; step7.1 makes it positive. This argument constructs the clutching bundle and uses integrality of its Chern class, not an unproved instanton profile or a classification of all bundles on $S^4$.

Let $k_\infty=-\langle c_2(P_\infty),[X]\rangle$. The extended bundle is smooth, so [F5] makes this an integer and $E(A_\infty)=8\pi^2k_\infty\ge0$. The same calculation gives $E(A_n)=8\pi^2k$ for every sequence member. Substitute step8.1 into step7.1 to get $k=k_\infty+\sum_pm_p$. A sequence with negative prescribed $k$ cannot exist by the energy formula. All claims about the smooth limit, gauges and integer loss are now established.

Specify the compactification and verify that no extra ideal data are required. An ideal connection is a smooth self-dual gauge orbit on a bundle of charge $j\ge0$, together with a finite unordered collection of points of total positive integer weight $k-j$. Its topology is the actual convergence of connections modulo smooth local comparison gauges off those points, together with weak convergence of the energy measure $|F|^2d\mathrm{vol}+8\pi^2\sum m\delta_p$. Steps1.1–9.1 prove that every original sequence has an ideal subsequential limit in this topology. The same proof works for a sequence of background bundles, since no fixed-bundle hypothesis was used before the comparison construction. For a sequence of ideal connections, first pass to a fixed background charge in the finite range $0,\ldots,k$. The finite point configurations have a convergent subsequence by compactness of $X$: list their finitely many repeated points, extract in $X$ and forget that listing. Apply steps1.1–9.1 to the background connections and add their new bubble weights to the limiting old weights at coincident points. The exact charge equation persists. Thus the ideal space, and in particular the closure of the original moduli, is sequentially compact.

For completeness this topology is second-countable and Hausdorff, so sequential compactness really gives compactness. Here is a countable local-data construction. Use the fixed countable coordinate-ball basis, finite deleted-ball lists and finite chart subcovers of their compact complements. Smooth potentials and smooth transition maps on each such finite arrangement have countable $C^r$ coefficient bases: use rational polynomial approximations on finitely many smaller boxes, smooth fixed cutoffs, rational tolerances and integer $r$. Their subspaces satisfying the unitary and transition identities inherit those bases. Arbitrary changes of local frames act by homeomorphisms, so the open saturations of these countable bases form a countable basis on the corresponding gauge quotients. Combine these tests with the countable uniform-dense family of continuous functions on compact $X$, constructed by the same rational-chart approximation, for the weak energy tests. Require also that all listed ideal points lie in the chosen deleted balls. That condition follows locally from finitely many open energy tests: outside those balls the limiting smooth energy measure has no atom, so cover the compact remainder by finitely many smaller balls with test-function integrals less than $4\pi^2$. For sufficiently close energy measures these integrals remain less than $8\pi^2$, excluding every positive integer ideal atom where a test function is one. Thus these saturated finite-chart and energy tests give a countable basis for exactly the convergence in step10.1. No classification of bundle isomorphism types or global Coulomb slice is used. For uniqueness of a limit, compare two proposed limits on the complement of their finite exceptional sets. Gauges between their smoothly convergent representatives satisfy $dh_n=h_nb_n-a_nh_n$. Unitarity and the smooth coefficient bounds control all gauge derivatives locally, so a diagonal gives a smooth limiting gauge intertwining the two background connections. Weak energy measures have unique limits against the continuous test functions, so their atomic weights and positions agree; the smooth background measure has no atoms. This gauge extends over every exceptional point: in their two smooth extension frames its derivative is bounded by the same equation, and the length distance on a punctured four-ball has the Euclidean completion, so it has a unique continuous limit at the puncture. The bounded derivative gives a weak Lipschitz extension, and the equation then bootstraps to smoothness. The ideal limits are therefore the same. With the countable neighborhood bases just constructed, failure of Hausdorff separation would select a point in every intersection of two shrinking neighborhood bases, giving a sequence with those two different limits. If no finite subcover existed, choose a point outside its first $n$ members; a convergent subsequence would contradict the member containing its limit. For $A\subseteq X$ there is an exact sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(A;G)\to H_n(X;G)\to H_n(X,A;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(A;G)\to H_{n-1}(X;G)\to\cdots.$$

Assume AC. Let $M$ be a compact $R$-oriented $n$-manifold with boundary $A$, for a commutative unital ring $R$. Cap with its relative fundamental class gives isomorphisms, for every integer $p$,
$$S_p:H^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M,A;R),\qquad T_p:H^p(M,A;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R).$$
Here both maps send a class $a$ to $a\cap[M,A]$ in the displayed target. Empty boundary recovers Poincaré duality. Disconnected and empty manifolds are included. AC is inherited only from the exhaustion and local universal-coefficient arguments in Poincaré duality.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Every smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M$ be a closed smooth
manifold ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Then $M$ has the homotopy type of a finite
CW complex ([[def-cw-complex-with-closure-finiteness-and-weak-topology]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $W$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold whose boundary $M$ is a rational homology three-sphere, meaning $H_*(M;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. The boundary intersection lattice has underlying group $L_W=H_2(W;\mathbb Z)/\operatorname{Tor}H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. Poincaré–Lefschetz duality identifies each $x\in H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$ with a class $\alpha_x\in H^2(W,M;\mathbb Z)$. Define $Q_W(\bar x,\bar y)=\langle\alpha_x\smile\alpha_y,[W,M]\rangle$, where $\smile$ is the relative cup product and $[W,M]\in H_4(W,M;\mathbb Z)$ is the relative orientation class; equivalently, this is the signed intersection number of interior two-cycle representatives. Its rank is $b_2(W)=\dim_{\mathbb Q}H_2(W;\mathbb Q)$. A nondegenerate positive-definite $Q_W$ is called a positive-definite filling lattice. It is not required to be unimodular; the boundary linking form can make its determinant have absolute value greater than one.

derivations.claim: The collar of $M$ lets every absolute two-cycle be moved into $\operatorname{int}W$. The signed transverse intersection number is integer-valued and bilinear. Since $H_2(M;\mathbb Q)=0$, [F1] shows that $H_2(W;\mathbb Q)\to H_2(W,M;\mathbb Q)$ is an isomorphism. [given, F1, F5, construct]

The pairing map over $\mathbb Q$ is the composite $H_2(W;\mathbb Q)\to H_2(W,M;\mathbb Q)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PD}^{-1}}H^2(W;\mathbb Q)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(H_2(W;\mathbb Q),\mathbb Q)$. Every map in this composite is an isomorphism by step 1.1, [F2], and [F3], so the form is rationally nondegenerate. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

By [F4] and [A1], $H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$ is finitely generated, so its torsion-free quotient is a finite-rank free abelian group. Any torsion class maps to zero over $\mathbb Q$, so the integral intersection pairing annihilates torsion in either variable and descends to this quotient. The four-dimensional cup-product sign is $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=+1$, so the form is symmetric. [F4, F5, A1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

Let $n\ge1$, let $L$ be a free abelian group of rank $n$ with an integer-valued symmetric bilinear form whose Gram determinant is $1$ or $-1$, and let $f:L\to\mathbb Z^n$ be an isometric homomorphism, where $\mathbb Z^n$ has its standard dot product. Then $f(L)=\mathbb Z^n$.

derivations.claim: Let $A_7$ be the $7\times7$ leading principal block on vertices $1,\ldots,7$. Its leading principal determinants $d_k$ satisfy $d_0=1$, $d_1=2$, and $d_k=2d_{k-1}-d_{k-2}$ for $2\le k\le7$, by expansion along the last row of the tridiagonal chain matrix. Induction gives $d_k=k+1$, so these seven determinants are positive. [F1, algebra, induction]

The vector $x=A_7^{-1}e_3$ has coordinates $x_i=\min(i,3)(8-\max(i,3))/8$ for $1\le i\le7$: substitution into $2x_i-x_{i-1}-x_{i+1}=\delta_{i3}$ with $x_0=x_8=0$ verifies $A_7x=e_3$. Hence $e_3^{\mathsf T}A_7^{-1}e_3=15/8$. The Schur-complement determinant of $C=\begin{pmatrix}A_7&-e_3\\-e_3^{\mathsf T}&2\end{pmatrix}$ is $\det(A_7)(2-15/8)=8/8=1$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

By Sylvester's criterion, the positive leading principal determinants $d_1,\ldots,d_7$ from step 1.1 and $\det C=1$ from step 1.2 make $C$ positive definite. For any $z\in\mathbb Z^8$, $z^{\mathsf T}Cz=2\sum_i z_i^2-2\sum_{\{i,j\}\text{ an edge}}z_i z_j$ is even. Every nonzero vector therefore has positive even integral norm, hence norm at least $2$; in particular there is no norm-one vector. [F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

The standard lattice $\mathbb Z^8$ contains norm-one basis vectors, so no isometry from $L_{E_8}$ onto $\mathbb Z^8$ exists by step 2.1. If there were an isometric full-rank embedding, its Gram determinant would be $1$ by step 1.2, and [F2] would force its image to be all of $\mathbb Z^8$, which would be an isometry, again contradicting step 2.1. [F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

The Hodge star on two-forms is $*$, and $F_A^-=(F_A-*F_A)/2$ denotes the anti-self-dual projection of the curvature of a connection $A$. The equation used in this item is $F_A^-=0$, so the curvature is self-dual; this convention and the negative second Chern number are fixed together for the positive-definite orientation. The self-dual moduli set is the set of smooth connections satisfying $F_A^-=0$, modulo the action of smooth gauge transformations of $P$. At a solution, the deformation complex is $0\to\Omega^0(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\xrightarrow{d_A}\Omega^1(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\xrightarrow{d_A^-}\Omega^-(X;\operatorname{ad}P)\to0$, and its gauge-fixed operator is $D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$. For index calculations, $D_A$ is completed from the first Sobolev space of one-forms to the direct sum of the zeroth Sobolev spaces of zero-forms and anti-self-dual two-forms.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed connected oriented smooth Riemannian four-manifold, let $b_1(X)=\dim H^1(X;\mathbb R)$, let $b_-(X)$ be the dimension of the negative subspace of its real intersection form, and let $P\to X$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle. Put $k=-\langle c_2(P),[X]\rangle$. For the real Fredholm operator $D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-$ from first Sobolev one-forms with values in $\operatorname{ad}P$ to zeroth Sobolev zero-forms and anti-self-dual two-forms, its Fredholm index is $8k-3(1-b_1(X)+b_-(X))$. In particular, if $\pi_1(X)=0$, the intersection form is positive definite, and $c_2(P)[X]=-1$, then $\operatorname{ind}_{\mathbb R}(D_A)=5$.

Assume full AC. Let $P$ be a smooth principal $SU(2)$-bundle over a connected closed Riemannian four-manifold $X$. Fix a smooth reference connection and use the corresponding finite-chart Sobolev norms. Let $\mathcal A^3$ be its affine $H^3$ space of connections, and let $\mathcal G^4$ be the group of $H^4$ sections of the bundle with fiber $SU(2)$ and conjugation transition maps. A connection is called irreducible when its stabilizer in this group is precisely the two constant central transformations. The irreducible locus is open. Its quotient $\mathcal B^*=\mathcal A^{3,*}/(\mathcal G^4/\{\pm1\})$ is a Hausdorff, second-countable smooth Hilbert manifold. At each irreducible $A$, a neighborhood is represented uniquely by a sufficiently small ball in $\ker(d_A^*:H^3(\Lambda^1\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)\to H^2(\operatorname{ad}P))$.

The corresponding quotient of $H^2(\Lambda^-\otimes\operatorname{ad}P)$ is a smooth Hilbert bundle over $\mathcal B^*$, with smooth curvature section $[A]\mapsto F_A^-$. Its slice linearization is $a\mapsto d_A^-a$. Fixing a point of $P$ above $x_0\in X$, quotienting instead by transformations with value $1$ there gives a principal $SO(3)$-bundle over $\mathcal B^*$. In local product coordinates the curvature section is its pullback. In particular its linearization has three additional kernel directions and the same cokernel; framing must not be identified with the unbased deformation problem.

Assume full AC. Use the unbased $H^3/H^4$ irreducible connection quotient on a closed Riemannian four-manifold and its $H^2$ anti-self-dual curvature bundle. Let $U$ be an open subset covered by finitely many Coulomb slices centered at smooth irreducible connections $A_i$. In each of these charts use a bounded open ball of radius $R_i$ in $S_i=\ker d_{A_i}^*\subset H^3$. Let $V$ be open, with its closure contained in the union of the images of smaller closed balls of radii $r_i<R_i$, all these images lying in $U$.

Allow smooth sections $\sigma$ supported in $U$, whose representatives in the specified charts are smooth maps into $H^3$ and have finite uniform $H^3$ norm on these chart balls. Interpret them in the $H^2$ equation bundle by inclusion. Give this class the topology generated by the uniform $H^3$ section norm on the finitely many chart balls and the $C^1(H^3,H^2)$ seminorms on compact subsets of those balls. Then the perturbations for which $\Phi+\sigma$, $\Phi([A])=F_A^-$, is transverse to zero at every zero in $\overline V$ form an open dense subset. The zero set in $V$ is a smooth finite-dimensional manifold of dimension equal to the unbased ASD index. In particular that dimension is five in the simply connected positive-definite charge $c_2=-1$ case.

Assume full AC. Let $X$ be a closed simply connected oriented Riemannian smooth four-manifold and $E$ a Hermitian rank-two bundle with fixed unit determinant. Over its affine $H^3$ space of determinant-one connections, consider the real Fredholm family
$$D_A=d_A^*\oplus d_A^-:H^3(\Lambda^1\otimes\mathfrak{su}(E))\longrightarrow H^2((\Lambda^0\oplus\Lambda^-)\otimes\mathfrak{su}(E)).$$
Its determinant line admits an orientation preserved by every $H^4$ determinant-one gauge transformation. It consequently descends to an orientable line bundle on the unbased irreducible quotient. The same assertion holds after any continuous gauge-equivariant family of compact perturbations of these operators. At the regular zero set of a smooth curvature perturbation with compact slice derivative, this orientation induces an orientation of the actual finite-dimensional moduli manifold. The orientation is not asserted to be canonical without additional choices.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Formula [F2] gives that index as five.

Apply [F4] with the exact finite larger and smaller slice balls in the Statement. It proves openness from a compact set containing every zero of all uniformly nearby perturbations, using the uniform $H^4$ bound; density is the finite cokernel-complement perturbation and finite-dimensional Sard argument. By [F5], the unperturbed real determinant line is orientable with every gauge transformation preserving the orientation. Scaling the compact perturbation derivative from zero to its actual value preserves this property. At a transverse zero the kernel of the slice derivative is the moduli tangent space and its cokernel is zero, so the determinant orientation gives a tangent orientation. The extra scalar gauge block is invertible and has its fixed orientation. Therefore the actual unbased moduli manifold is orientable. The based quotient only pulls this construction back and adds the three framing directions described in [F3]; it is not used to change the index in step 1.1. This proves all conclusions.

$$\|f\|_\sharp=\sup_{x\in X}\int_XG(x,y)|f(y)|\,dV_y,\qquad \|f\|_B=\|f\|_\sharp+\|f\|_2.$$
Complete the smooth sections of $\Lambda^-\otimes\operatorname{ad}P$ in this norm. There are $\varepsilon_0,C>0$, depending only on $X,g,c,\Lambda$, with the following property for every smooth $SU(2)$ connection $A$ on any smooth bundle $P$ over $X$. Suppose
$$\langle P_A\xi,\xi\rangle\ge c\|\xi\|_2^2,\quad P_A=d_A^-(d_A^-)^*,\quad \|F_A\|_2\le\Lambda,\quad E=F_A^-,\quad\|E\|_B\le\varepsilon_0.$$
Then $Q_A=(d_A^-)^*P_A^{-1}$ is defined on the actual completed space and satisfies
$$\|(Q_Af\wedge Q_Ah)^-\|_B\le C\|f\|_B\|h\|_B.$$
For $\xi=P_A^{-1}f$ and $a=Q_Af$, it also satisfies
$$\|\xi\|_\infty\le C\|f\|_\sharp,\quad \|\nabla_A^2\xi\|_2+\|a\|_4+\|\nabla_Aa\|_2\le C\|f\|_B,\quad \bigl\||a|^2\bigr\|_\sharp\le C\|f\|_\sharp^2.$$
The equation $f=-E-(Q_Af\wedge Q_Af)^-$ has a unique solution in the closed radius-$2\|E\|_B$ ball. It gives a smooth self-dual connection $A+Q_Af$ on the same smooth bundle, with all the displayed correction norms at most $C\|E\|_B$. No uniform bound on derivatives of $F_A$ or on local coefficients of $A$ is assumed.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary, of real dimension at least two. Its metric defines the $L^2$ pairing on forms by the Riemannian density; orientation is unnecessary. Let $d^*$ denote the formal adjoint of $d$, and $\Delta=dd^*+d^*d$ on total real forms, or on their complexification. With domain $H^2$ the operator is nonnegative and selfadjoint. Its degreewise smooth kernels $\mathcal H^k$ are finite dimensional, and there is an orthogonal smooth decomposition
$$\Omega^k(M)=\mathcal H^k\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d\Omega^{k-1}(M)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}d^*\Omega^{k+1}(M).$$
The map $h\mapsto[h]$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal H^k\to H^k_{\mathrm{dR}}(M)$, over $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$ as appropriate.

More generally let $X$ be a compact complex manifold of complex dimension $m\ge1$ with a smooth Hermitian metric. Let $E$ be a holomorphic bundle of finite rank with a smooth Hermitian metric. The holomorphic bundle structure supplies frames with holomorphic invertible transition matrices; the Hermitian metric is separate smooth positive-definite pairing data. On $E$-valued $(p,q)$ forms, define $\bar\partial_E$ by the coefficientwise Dolbeault operator in holomorphic bundle charts and let $\bar\partial_E^*$ be its formal adjoint. For each fixed $p$, $\Delta_{\bar\partial_E}=\bar\partial_E\bar\partial_E^*+\bar\partial_E^*\bar\partial_E$ on the sum over $q$ is nonnegative and selfadjoint on $H^2$; its smooth harmonic spaces $\mathcal H_E^{p,q}$ are finite dimensional and
$$\Omega^{p,q}(X,E)=\mathcal H_E^{p,q}\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E\Omega^{p,q-1}(X,E)\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\bar\partial_E^*\Omega^{p,q+1}(X,E).$$
In particular harmonic forms represent the smooth Dolbeault quotient
$$H_{\bar\partial}^{p,q}(X,E):=\ker\bar\partial_E/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_E$$
uniquely. Terms outside the degree range are zero. This asserts smooth Dolbeault cohomology; an identification with sheaf cohomology requires a separate Dolbeault-resolution comparison theorem.

For either complex write $D=d$ or $D=\bar\partial_E$, $P=DD^*+D^*D$, and let $\Pi,G$ be the preceding Green projection and inverse. They preserve degree, $G$ preserves smooth forms, and on smooth forms
$$DG=GD,\qquad D^*G=GD^*,\qquad D\Pi=\Pi D=D^*\Pi=\Pi D^*=0.$$
Every closed smooth $u$ satisfies $u=\Pi u+D(D^*Gu)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $M,E,P$ have exactly the compact, boundaryless, scalar-positive-symbol and formal symmetry hypotheses of [[thm-elliptic-differential-operators-on-compact-vector-bundles-have-parametrices-and-regularity]], with $\operatorname{dom}P=H^2(M,E)$. Write $\mathcal H=\ker P$.

Then $\mathcal H$ is finite dimensional and consists of smooth sections, $\operatorname{ran}P=\mathcal H^\perp$ is closed in $L^2$, and
$$L^2(M,E)=\mathcal H\mathbin{\oplus^\perp}\operatorname{ran}P.$$
Let $\Pi$ be the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal H$. There is a unique linear operator $G:L^2\to H^2\cap\mathcal H^\perp$ with
$$PG=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }L^2,\qquad GP=I-\Pi\quad\hbox{on }H^2,\qquad G\Pi=\Pi G=0.$$
It is bounded from $H^k$ to $H^{k+2}$ for every integer $k\ge0$, compact and selfadjoint on $L^2$, and preserves smooth sections. For all such $k$,
$$H^k=\mathcal H\oplus P(H^{k+2}),\qquad C^\infty(M,E)=\mathcal H\oplus P(C^\infty(M,E)),$$
where the second summands are the corresponding intersections with $\mathcal H^\perp$, and the decompositions are topological. The projection is smoothing: for every integer $r\ge0$, $\|\Pi f\|_{C^r}\le C_r\|f\|_2$. Consequently $G$ is a two-sided parametrix with finite-rank smoothing remainders. If additionally $(Pu,u)_2\ge0$ for smooth $u$, then $P$ and $G$ are nonnegative on their respective domains.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $p,q\in[1,\infty]$ be
conjugate exponents, and let $f,g$ be measurable real-valued functions.

1. If $1\le p<\infty$ and $q<\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^p(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^q(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_p\|g\|_q.$$
2. If $p=1$ and $q=\infty$ with $f\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$ and
   $g\in L^\infty(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_1\|g\|_\infty.$$
3. If $p=\infty$ and $q=1$ with $f\in L^\infty(\mu)$ and
   $g\in\mathcal L^1(\mu)$, then
   $$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_\infty\|g\|_1.$$

In every case the right-hand side is finite, so $fg$ is integrable.

Assume full Axiom of Choice. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Hausdorff
second-countable smooth manifold, possibly with boundary or empty, and let
$\rho_M:H^*(M;\mathbb Z)\to H^*(M;\mathbb R)$ be induced by
$\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb R$. Write $J_M$ for the natural de Rham
isomorphism from real de Rham cohomology to singular cohomology with real
coefficients.

For every finite-rank smooth complex bundle $E\to M$ with a Hermitian metric
and Hermitian connection $\nabla$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([c_j(\nabla)])=\rho_M(c_j(E)).$$
For every finite-rank smooth real bundle $V\to M$ with any real connection
$D$, and every $j\geq0$,
$$J_M([p_j(D)])=\rho_M(p_j(V)).$$
For every oriented Euclidean bundle $W\to M$ of even rank with a
metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, and its Thom-normalized Euler class,
$$J_M([e(\nabla)])=\rho_M(e(W)).$$
Here $c_j(\nabla)$, $p_j(D)$, and $e(\nabla)$ use the normalizations in
[[def-chern-pontryagin-and-euler-characteristic-forms]], while $c_j(E)$,
$p_j(V)$, and $e(W)$ are the published topological classes. In particular
$c_1(L)=e(L_{\mathbb R})$ for a complex line and
$p_j(V)=(-1)^j c_{2j}(V_{\mathbb C})$. These are equalities after passage to
real coefficients; no equality with integral torsion is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and
the ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is
dispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second
countable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\infty)^c\times\mathbb R^{n-c}$
and transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner
points; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be
compact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.
Corner faces are locally subpolyhedra, and any specified finite union of
closed faces is a subpolyhedron.

If the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation
$f:L\to\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its
differential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the
tangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise
